Attackers can submit an endpoint .example .mozaws.net/push, which passes validation while Go parses the actual host as…

item.title: Pam: linux-pam pam econf local privilege escalation via relative "(null)" config directory from empty vendor directory handling
item.description: A flaw was found in pam. When built with libeconf and an unconfigured vendor directory, the pam econf configuration handler misinterprets the search path, causing it to look for configuration files in a relative directory within the current working directory. A local attacker can exploit this by placing crafted environment configuration files in a world-writable location. If an administrator executes a privileged…

When started with Streamable HTTP transport and --api-key, the server binds 0.0.0.0…

item.title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Unsandboxed DuckDB SQL Execution via query messages
item.description: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 exposes unsandboxed DuckDB SQL execution through the read-only annotated query messages MCP tool, allowing file access and network requests. Attackers who prompt-inject the driving LLM via recorded logs or topics can invoke read csv auto, COPY TO, or httpfs to read and write files and perform server-side request forgery.

item.title: Bagel before 2.5.5 Argument Injection via rsync Pipeline Task Options
item.description: Bagel (bagel-mcp) before 2.5.5 contains an argument injection vulnerability in RsyncFilesToLocalDirectory that allows attackers to inject rsync options because only --quiet and --log-format values are rejected. Attackers who influence the LLM through prompt-injected content can trigger run pipeline with -e/--rsh or --rsync-path options to execute commands as the Bagel server process.

item.title: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 SSRF via blueteam check webshell Hostname Bypass
item.description: Wazuh-MCP-Server before commit 2bbfe12 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the blueteam check webshell tool because WebshellCheckInput.validate url accepts DNS hostnames without resolving them. Attackers can supply URLs whose hostnames resolve or redirect to loopback, private, or link-local addresses, making curl reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints and leak response details.

item.title: SylphxAI pdf-reader-mcp 2.4.1 through 3.1.4 SSRF via DNS Rebinding in URL Loader
item.description: SylphxAI pdf-reader-mcp 2.4.1 through 3.0.14, 3.0.16, and 3.1.2 through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in its PDF URL loader, which validates the resolved address but does not pin it for fetch(). Attackers controlling DNS for a url passed to read pdf can return a public address at check time and an internal address at connection time to reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

item.title: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 Cross-Workspace Webhook Disclosure via Unscoped webhookId
item.description: Typebot from 2.14.0 before 3.19.0 contains an authorization flaw that allows authenticated bot authors to reference another workspace's legacy webhook by saving a foreign webhookId in an HTTP request block. Attackers can have executeHttpRequestBlock return the victim's URL, headers and body client-side, or use handleSubscribeHttpRequest to overwrite the victim's webhook URL and redirect its data.

item.title: WhoDB 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 MCP Read-Only Bypass via Server-Side File Writes
item.description: WhoDB from 0.88.0 before 0.132.0 contains an access control bypass in the MCP whodb query tool, letting callers run file-writing statements without approval because the sqlguard keyword classifier omits INTO, OUTFILE and DUMPFILE. MCP clients or prompt-injected models can execute PostgreSQL lo export or MySQL SELECT INTO OUTFILE to create files on the database host and create tables, bypassing confirmation and…

item.title: Apache Airflow Reflected Cross-site Scripting vulnerability in 404 Endpoint
item.description: It was noticed an XSS in certain 404 pages that could be exploited to perform an XSS attack. Chrome will detect this as a reflected XSS attempt and prevent the page from loading. However Firefox and other browsers don't, and are vulnerable to this attack. Mitigation: The fix for this is to upgrade to Apache Airflow 1.9.0 or above.

item.title: DOMPurify allows tampering by prototype pollution
item.description: It has been discovered that malicious HTML using special nesting techniques can bypass the depth checking added to DOMPurify in recent releases. It was also possible to use Prototype Pollution to weaken the depth check. This renders dompurify unable to avoid XSS attack. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify envelope bsp()…
